Supreme Court Reserves Verdict on PMLA Authority's Powers

The Supreme Court has reserved its verdict on whether a single-member, non-judicial authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) can confirm property attachment orders issued by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). During the hearings, senior advocate Vikram Chaudhri, appearing for the petitioners, argued that the Adjudicating Authority (AA) performs a quasi-judicial function, not an administrative one, as it is required to decide on provisional attachments within 180 days. The core of the legal debate centers on the composition and powers of this authority in relation to judicial oversight.
